question.problem:
$$
(\,∀y\in (0,1),\,{{x}^{2}}_{\begin{aligned} \\ ↑ \\ \text{I}\end{aligned}}-{y}^{2}\ge 0\,)⇒(\,∃{z}_{\begin{aligned} \\ ↑ \\ \text{II}\end{aligned}}\in Q,\,z={{y}^{2}}_{\begin{aligned} \\ ↑ \\ \text{III}\end{aligned}}\,)
$$

Which occurrences of the variables in the expression above are free?
question.worked_solution:
Let's examine our expression and mark the occurrences of the variables as bound $(\text{b})$ or free $(\text{f}).$

- Occurrence I of the variable $x$ is *free* since it isn't placed right next to a quantifier and it doesn't lie within the scope of a quantifier that uses $x.$

- Occurrence II of the variable $z$ is *bound* since it is placed right next to the quantifier $∃:$

$$
(∀y\in (0,1),\,{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}\ge 0\,)⇒(\,∃\,{z}_{\begin{aligned} \\ ↑ \\ \text{b}\end{aligned}}\in Q,\,z={y}^{2}\,)
$$

- Occurrence III of the variable $y$ is *free* since it isn't placed right next to a quantifier and it doesn't lie within the scope of a quantifier that uses $y.$

The occurrences of variables in the expression are as follows:

$$
(\,∀{y}_{\begin{aligned} \\ ↑ \\ \text{b}\end{aligned}}\in (0,1),\,{{x}^{2}}_{\begin{aligned} \\ ↑ \\ \text{f}\end{aligned}}-{{y}^{2}}_{\begin{aligned} \\ ↑ \\ \text{b}\end{aligned}}\ge 0\,)⇒(\,∃{z}_{\begin{aligned} \\ ↑ \\ \text{b}\end{aligned}}\in Q,\,{z}_{\begin{aligned} \\ ↑ \\ \text{b}\end{aligned}}={{y}^{2}}_{\begin{aligned} \\ ↑ \\ \text{f}\end{aligned}}\,)
$$

Therefore, the free occurrence is "I and III only."
